authority: Director requested completed appearance after accepting dimensions; construction blockouts are internal checks, not a new approval gate.
workflow: Controlled native geometry targets followed by sketch-to-render appearance finishing. Not a third free-form composition revision.

approval_evidence.scope: Accept the three completed appearance images for the next comparative roster review. No production model, native geometry fidelity, animation, gameplay change or complete T082 corpus acceptance.

limitations: Native dimensions and foundation equality do not prove raster dimensions or pixel-identical foundations.
Raster molded-part seams and embossed LEGO stud lettering are generated interpretations, not official product or physical-buildability evidence.
No gameplay import, GLB, production rig, LOD or playable-build update.

assets.prompt:
Use case: sketch-to-render.
Asset type: finished LEGO Space RTS visual concept for director review, NOT an intermediate blockout.
Image 1 is the exact construction/proportion target, from a native 3D model. Image 2 is official LEGO Mars Mission construction/material style reference only, NOT a layout to copy.
Finish image 1 as a convincing completed LEGO toy-scale model product render. Preserve its overall footprint, relative height, major masses, connected modules, camera and subject count. Replace faceted CAD-looking surfaces with recognizable broad molded LEGO curved slopes, wedge plates, attached roots, a few full-size connection studs and physically readable simple joins. Do NOT merely recolor the primitive model. Do NOT add dense geometry. Construction complexity comparable to official small/medium Mars Mission models: large simple pieces, not layered sci-fi greebles.
Use source-family black armor, restrained opaque lime molded inserts, dark-gray connected structure, transparent yellow-green small energy interfaces, and a few recessed pale internal support / dark-green living links. Living links only in narrow protected structural slots, not exposed skin, machine hydraulics, loose tentacles or decorative veins. Opaque lime never glows.
Neutral light gray studio backdrop, clean soft light, readable black surfaces, subject fills frame with modest margin, grounded soft contact shadow or visible worker hover clearance. Completed crisp product/concept render, no cinematic environment, no typography, no logos, no watermarks, no pilot, no extra props. Do not increase detail to create polish.
Subject: ETX Servitor, a small uncrewed economic hover worker for ore/crystal collection, construction and repair; NOT a combat craft or humanoid robot.
Invariants: Body 6x8 connector-grid units, only 8 plates high, overall length 10 with the SHORT two-jaw utility clamp. Two broad connected side shell valves enclose a low body and narrow protected support slot. Finish the mouth as a convincing attached paired molded utility clamp, NOT guns or a human robot arm. Retain four large rear connection studs, not rows of studs. The whole craft is small minifigure-scale. Closed uncrewed hull, no cockpit/seat/alien rider, no legs, no weapons, no crystal permanently attached to body. Donor reference supplies small-chassis simplicity, NOT its pilot or lime rider arches. The two valves should read as compact molded curved shell pieces rather than two massive plain bricks. No StarCraft drone or generic present-day machine.
